name: Ditto
sounds_sub: Eight short pieces, each one factory program played as the FM-1 plays it: one sampler, its eight voices, its arpeggiator, delay and reverb. No effects added afterwards.
tagline: An eighties sampler for the M-VAVE FM-1, after the E-mu Emulator II: two sounds layered, eight bits, an analog filter.
lead: The FM-1 as a sampler of the mid-eighties, after the Emulator II and as dry as it was: a library of sixteen sounds, one or two on every note, through an 8-bit companded sample player into a 24 dB filter and a VCA, each with its ADSR, and one LFO. A grey panel, a two-line LCD, modules and their numbered functions.

device_sub: The buttons are the Emulator II's modules: GLO the MASTER, SCL the FILTER, ENV the LFO/VCA, EDIT the VOICE DEFINITION, SEQ the PRESET DEFINITION, REC the SEQUENCER, FX the effects, SAVE the DISK. Press a module again for its next function; KNOB 1–4 are the four sliders; the LCD says where you are.
features_sub: One sampler voice, the Emulator II's, with 32 presets.

features.p: Strings, a choir, an orchestra hit, piano, brass, flute, cellos, organ, harpsichord, marimba, tubular bells, pizzicato, double bass, timpani, a breathy recorder, harp: 41 zones from CC0 recordings. Three slots for your own samples.
PRESET DEF assigns SOUND B, as the Emulator II's presets did: stacked, VELOCITY SWITCH, VELOCITY CROSSFADE, a SPLIT or a POSITIONAL CROSSFADE over a range of keys.
EII: 8-bit μ-law and no interpolation, the grain of the Emulator II. Or CLEAN, the recordings as they are.
A 24 dB low-pass with its ADSR, a VCA with its ADSR, one LFO with a delay to the pitch, the filter and the level; velocity to the level and the filter. No patch bay: the routings are the EII's.
The notes start further into the sample, past its attack; a sustained sound loops while the key is held, or plays once through.
A two-line LCD in 5 × 7 dots, four sliders and the modules' LEDs: the functions numbered as on the instrument (FILTER 1, VOICE DEF 21, PRESET DEF 25).
An arpeggiator in PRESET DEF, as on the EII; a small 16-step sequencer with ties, accents and slides, its steps drawn on the LCD.
Only these two, as one would have patched them in 1984: a stereo delay in time with the tempo and a room, spring or hall reverb.
24 factory sounds (STRINGS, CHOIR, ORCH HIT, PIANO, SHAKUHACHI, BOW + PLUCK, BASS / PIANO, BRASS / HIT, CELLO>CHOIR…) and eight free slots. MIDI Program Change picks them.
